# 1955 in music - Wikipedia

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Pete_Seeger_NYWTS.jpg/250px-Pete_Seeger_NYWTS.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pete_Seeger_NYWTS.jpg)

[Pete Seeger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Seeger "Pete Seeger") in 1955

*   [1955 in country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_in_country_music "1955 in country music")
*   [1955 in jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_in_jazz "1955 in jazz")

*   [January 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_1 "January 1") – [RCA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Corporation "RCA Corporation") Victor announces a marketing plan called "Operation TNT." The label drops the list price on LPs from $5.95 to $3.98, EPs from $4.95 to $2.98, 45 EPs from $1.58 to $1.49 and 45's from $1.16 to $.89. Other record labels follow RCA's lead and begin to drop prices as well.
*   [January 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_7 "January 7")
    *   [Marian Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marian_Anderson "Marian Anderson") is the first [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American") singer to perform at the [Metropolitan Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Opera "Metropolitan Opera") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").
    *   "[Rock Around the Clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Around_the_Clock "Rock Around the Clock")" by [Bill Haley & His Comets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Haley_&_His_Comets "Bill Haley & His Comets") first appears on the British charts.
*   [January 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_14 "January 14") – In New York City, [Alan Freed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Freed "Alan Freed") produces the first [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") concert.
*   [January 27](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_27 "January 27") – [Michael Tippett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Tippett "Michael Tippett")'s opera _[The Midsummer Marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Midsummer_Marriage "The Midsummer Marriage")_ is premiered at the [Royal Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Opera_House "Royal Opera House"), Covent Garden in London, conducted by [John Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Pritchard_\(conductor\) "John Pritchard (conductor)"), with designs by [Barbara Hepworth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Hepworth "Barbara Hepworth") and choreography by [John Cranko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cra
*   [February 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_19 "February 19") – Dot Records introduces a new singer, [Pat Boone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Boone "Pat Boone"), with an advertisement in _Billboard_ magazine calling him "a great new voice". His first record for Dot Records is "Two Hearts, Two Kisses, One Love."
*   [February 24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_24 "February 24") – [Carlisle Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlisle_Floyd "Carlisle Floyd")'s opera _[Susannah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susannah "Susannah")_ is premiered in the Ruby Diamond Auditorium of [Florida State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_University "Florida State University"), [Tallahassee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallahassee,_Florida "Tallahassee, Florida") with [Phyllis Curtin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllis_Curtin "Phyllis Curtin") in the title role.
*   [March 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_7 "March 7") – The [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") production of [_Peter Pan_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Pan_\(1954_musical\) "Peter Pan (1954 musical)"), starring [Mary Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Martin "Mary Martin"), is presented on American television for the first time by [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")\-TV with its original cast, as an installment of _[Producers' Showcase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Producers'_Showcase "Producers' Showcase")_. It is also the first time that a stage musical is presented in its entirety on TV almost exactly as it was
*   [March 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_15 "March 15") – [Colonel Tom Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_Tom_Parker "Colonel Tom Parker") becomes [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley")'s _de facto_ manager.
*   [March 19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_19 "March 19") – The film _[Blackboard Jungle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackboard_Jungle "Blackboard Jungle")_ is premièred in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), featuring [Bill Haley & His Comets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Haley_&_His_Comets "Bill Haley & His Comets")' "[Rock Around the Clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Around_the_Clock "Rock Around the Clock")" over the opening credits, the first use of a rock and roll song in a major film.
    *   [Pierre Boulez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Boulez "Pierre Boulez")'s influential composition _[Le marteau sans maître](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_marteau_sans_ma%C3%AEtre "Le marteau sans maître")_ ("The hammer without a master"), for [contralto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contralto "Contralto") and six instrumentalists, is premiered (in its first revised version) at the [International Society for Contemporary Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Society_for_Contemporary_Music "International Society for Contemporary Music") Festival in [Baden-Baden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baden-Baden "Baden-Baden") at the insistence of [Heinrich Strobel](https:
*   [July 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/July_9 "July 9") – "Rock Around the Clock" becomes the first [Rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") single to reach Number One on the American charts.
*   [August 31](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_31 "August 31") – A Londoner is fined for "creating an abominable noise" for playing "[Shake, Rattle, and Roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake,_Rattle,_and_Roll "Shake, Rattle, and Roll")" at top volume.
*   [September 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_3 "September 3") – [Little Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Richard "Little Richard") records "[Tutti Frutti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutti_Frutti_\(song\) "Tutti Frutti (song)")" in New Orleans with significantly cleaned up lyrics (originally "Tutti Frutti, good booty" among other things); it is released in October.
*   [November 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_20 "November 20") – [Bo Diddley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Diddley "Bo Diddley") makes his debut TV appearance on _[The Ed Sullivan Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ed_Sullivan_Show "The Ed Sullivan Show")_ on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") television.
*   [November 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_22 "November 22") – Colonel Tom Parker signs [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley") to [RCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCA_Records "RCA Records").
*   [November 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_29 "November 29") – [Juan José Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Jos%C3%A9_Castro "Juan José Castro") conducts the UK première of [Carlos Chávez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Ch%C3%A1vez "Carlos Chávez")'s [Symphony No. 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphony_No._3_\(Ch%C3%A1vez\) "Symphony No. 3 (Chávez)") at the [Maida Vale Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maida_Vale_Studios "Maida Vale Studios") with the [London Symphony Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Symphony_Orchestra "London Symphony Orchestra").
*   [December 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/December_15 "December 15") – Sun Records releases "[Folsom Prison Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folsom_Prison_Blues "Folsom Prison Blues")" recorded by [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash") on July 30.
*   Publication of _[Neue Mozart-Ausgabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neue_Mozart-Ausgabe "Neue Mozart-Ausgabe")_ begins.

In 1955, 1,615 albums and 4,542 pop singles were released in the US.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_in_music#cite_note-4)
